solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Do this again showing tenacity! (7)

annotation.definitionNote: RESOLVE is the noun meaning tenacity; 'showing' links it to the first definition

blocks.note: 'this' is the clue itself; working it out a second time puts RE- before the verb for working out
determination, firmness of purpose, the noun

annotation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to try again and keep at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This' is the clue itself: to solve it again is to RE-SOLVE, which splits the word in a way the ear never does.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: firm determination, the quality of holding on through difficulty, is tenacity.

entries.clue: Why you shouldn’t trust salesman’s answers? (7)

blocks.note: the reason not to trust him: he lies

annotation.surface: A cynical question about whether a salesman's answers can be believed.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence, REP LIES, 'the rep lies', and the reason for distrust spells the answer. The 's stands for 'is', joining that sentence to 'answers'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name responses someone gives back after being questioned.

entries.clue: Possibly cork pieces finally on hat (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, S sits on top of TOPPER

blocks.note: a topper is a top hat

annotation.surface: Bits of cork stuck on a hat, like the corks dangling from an Australian bush hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags cork as one example of a stopper, not the only kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A cork is one sort of stopper, something that closes a bottle.

entries.clue: Reel turns making circles (5)

indicatorNotes.turns: a spool turned round reads backwards

annotation.surface: A spinning reel of line winding round in circles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like the reel spinning, but it is the instruction to run SPOOL backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a length of rope or wire bent round to meet itself forms these rings.

entries.clue: Government kill with intravenous injection (9)

annotation.surface: A state putting prisoners to death by lethal injection.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is grimly apt, since lethal injection is an execution method, and 'injection' does double duty as the insertion instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The executive is the branch of government that carries out the laws.

entries.clue: Culture perhaps found in V&A? (7)

blocks.note: literature and learning, a scholarly kind of culture
V and A are both characters of the alphabet

annotation.surface: Culture on show at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
annotation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum, a home of culture, but here it is just two letters of the alphabet with an ampersand.
annotation.definitionFit: Letters means literature and learning, as in 'a man of letters', one form of culture.

entries.clue: The French welcome time off (5)

annotation.surface: French people welcoming a holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: AVE is the Latin greeting, as in 'Ave Maria'.
annotation.definitionFit: Leave is permitted time off work or duty.

entries.clue: Clothes stoutly made, top to toe (9)

indicatorNotes.top to toe: the top letter of a down entry moves to the bottom

blocks.note: strapping = sturdily built; its S then moves to the end

annotation.surface: Garments sewn sturdily from head to foot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top to toe' sounds like dressing someone from head to foot, but in a down clue it moves the S of STRAPPING from top to bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Trappings are ornamental dress or outward accessories, so clothes.

entries.clue: Part of continent entering agreement (7)

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is part of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the run starts at the tail of 'continent' and ends inside 'entering'

annotation.surface: A region of Europe signing up to a treaty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the Entente Cordiale, the 1904 agreement between Britain and France on the continent.
annotation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations.

entries.clue: Top spot for water sport expert? (7)

annotation.surface: The best place for a keen surfer to be.
annotation.walkthrough: The surfer really does belong on the surface of the water, so the answer sits inside the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: The outermost layer of water or anything else is its uppermost part, hence a top spot.

entries.clue: Suggest it’s dull speaking about work (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so PROSE stands around OP

blocks.note: prose = dull, commonplace talk, as in prosaic

annotation.surface: A remark that talking about one's job is boring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' is OP, short for opus, not a job.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean putting forward an idea or plan for others to consider.

entries.clue: Plug more suitable for electrical device (7)

blocks.note: a plug = an advert, a piece of promotion

annotation.surface: Choosing a better plug for an electrical gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plug' sits right beside 'electrical device' pretending to be a wall plug, but it is AD, a plug in the advertising sense.
annotation.definitionFit: An adapter is a device connecting incompatible electrical plugs and sockets.

entries.clue: Fraud is shameless taking over street (9)

indicatorNotes.taking: IMPURE takes O and ST inside it

annotation.surface: A verdict that a swindle is brazen and shameless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shameless' needs the moral sense, not brazen, and 'over' comes from cricket scoring.
annotation.definitionFit: An imposture is a deception by pretending to be someone else, a fraud.

entries.clue: Animal also carried by father (5)

indicatorNotes.carried by: what is carried by something is held within it, so PA holds AND

annotation.surface: A child's toy animal carried along by Dad.
annotation.walkthrough: P(AND)A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this black-and-white bear from China is one kind of animal.

entries.clue: Be quiet and clean getting broom? (5)

annotation.surface: Doing the housework silently with a broom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broom' sits among cleaning words as a brush, but it is the yellow-flowered shrub, and the question mark admits the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: broom is a yellow-flowered bush, so one kind of woody garden plant.

entries.clue: Butterfly following borders with colour (9)

annotation.surface: A butterfly trailing after flower borders full of colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' suggests garden flower beds, where butterflies go, but it means edges. The brimstone is a yellow European butterfly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this sulphur-yellow species, named after the old word for sulphur, is one kind of butterfly.

entries.clue: Concerning to admit past is false (9)

indicatorNotes.to admit: to admit is to let in, so IN RE lets SINCE into its middle

blocks.note: in re = concerning, the legal Latin
since = ago, in the past, as in 'long since'

annotation.surface: Owning up to one's history as a lie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' is not the familiar two-letter abbreviation but the fuller legal Latin phrase, which splits into two words to let the past in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who pretends to feelings they lack is being false.

entries.clue: Supported American with tinted exterior (9)

indicatorNotes.exterior: STAINED forms the outside, around US

annotation.surface: An American propped up by someone with tanned or dyed skin.
annotation.walkthrough: S(US)TAINED.
annotation.definitionFit: To sustain is to hold up or support.

entries.clue: Preparation of feasts inside uncovered fat (9)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' places the feasts within the trimmed fat, so DINES sits in REAS
indicatorNotes.uncovered: GREASY loses its outer letters, G and Y

annotation.surface: Getting a banquet ready, with bare fat on the cook's board.
annotation.walkthrough: REA(DINES)S. 'Fat' is the adjective GREASY, not the noun, and 'uncovered' strips its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being prepared is the state that preparation brings about.

entries.clue: Stopped working and went to bed (7)

blocks.note: gave up one's job for good, typically at pension age
retire = go to bed for the night

annotation.surface: Someone clocking off and heading to bed.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves describe one tired evening, which hides that each alone defines the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Retired means gave up work; it also means withdrew to bed.

entries.clue: They won’t stand for old people! (7)

annotation.definition: They won’t stand for old people!

blocks.note: the surface reads this as refusing to get up and offer a seat; the setter means refusing to tolerate
the elderly as the target of a prejudice, not as passengers needing a seat

annotation.surface: Young passengers refusing to give up a seat to the elderly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Won't stand for' reads as refusing to rise from a seat for the elderly; it means won't tolerate them.
annotation.definitionFit: Ageists are prejudiced against people because of age, especially the old.

entries.clue: Greek character captured in water colour (5)

indicatorNotes.captured in: something captured in a thing is held inside it, so SEA holds PI

annotation.surface: A Greek figure painted in a watercolour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water colour' reads as one art term, but it splits: 'water' is SEA and 'colour' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, named after cuttlefish ink.

entries.clue: Tease is acceptable in show (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places OK within PROVE, as a thing is in its container

annotation.surface: Whether a striptease is allowed in a stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: PROV(OK)E. 'Show' is the verb, to demonstrate, not a stage performance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taunting someone to get a reaction is goading or teasing them.

entries.clue: Part is tempting absorbing performer (7)

indicatorNotes.absorbing: the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the run starts at the second letter of 'part' and ends two letters into 'tempting'

annotation.surface: An actor drawn in by a juicy role.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is theatrical throughout, a part tempting a performer, so it hides that the answer lies within the first three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a professional singer or dancer on stage is a performer; the French-derived word is used for entertainers.

entries.clue: Bands settle back covering Queen (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: what covers something wraps round it, so TIS wraps round ER

annotation.surface: Pop groups settling their backing arrangements with the band Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: TI(ER)S. 'Bands' and 'Queen' together suggest the rock group, but bands here are layers or ranks.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or layers, bands one above another.

entries.clue: Rapture seeing sunset’s end passed pool? (9)

blocks.note: pool, the cue game, is an example of a sport

annotation.surface: Delight at a sunset over a swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that pool is just one sport. 'Transport' is also a state of ecstasy, as in 'transports of delight'.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense: being carried away by strong feeling, as in 'transports of joy', is rapture.

entries.clue: Spoil sweetheart in Italian eatery (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the heart letter within TRAT, as a diner sits in a restaurant

annotation.surface: Pampering a lover over dinner at an Italian restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is not a lover: split it into sweet + heart, the middle letter of the word. A trat is British slang for an Italian trattoria.
annotation.definitionFit: To treat someone is to spoil them with something special.

entries.clue: Stem carrying grain of rice paddy (5)

indicatorNotes.carrying: a thing carrying something holds it within, so STOP holds R
indicatorNotes.grain of: a single grain, the first letter, of 'rice'

annotation.surface: A rice plant's stalk standing in a paddy field.
annotation.walkthrough: ST(R)OP. 'Paddy' begs to be the rice field, but it is the British word for a fit of temper, and a strop is the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A strop and a paddy are both British words for a sulk or tantrum.

entries.clue: Start to roast one’s fish croquette (7)

annotation.surface: Cooking instructions for a fishcake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I (the Roman one) plus 'S.
annotation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish, a croquette.

entries.clue: Tapers point with pointed missiles (7)

annotation.surface: Sharpening candles or arrows to a point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tapers' looks like the noun, thin candles, beside all the pointed things; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To taper is to narrow gradually towards one end.

entries.clue: Socialist’s leader in fitting decline (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the leader within the fitting, so S goes into DECENT

annotation.surface: A political party's leader stepping down with proper grace.
annotation.walkthrough: DE(S)CENT. 'Leader' looks like a party boss, but it only takes the S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a going down, whether downhill or in fortune, is a decline.

entries.clue: Cut out employing power drain (7)

indicatorNotes.employing: DELETE takes P into its body

annotation.surface: An electrical fault using up power until it drains away.
annotation.walkthrough: DE(P)LETE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: using up reserves until little is left is draining them.
